relations.evidence: If a user name string begins with role: then the remainder of the string is interpreted as a role name. There's no ambiguity here, because ":" is an illegal character in a user or role name.

cross_product_finding: The sync function is the headline structural departure for this batch: it is imperative JavaScript (ES5), executed per-document-revision, that combines validation, access-control grants, and document routing in one place - versus server/'s static named-privilege-to-operation table and Capella's static role-to-privilege grants, both of which are declarative and evaluated at request time against a fixed catalog. Its helper functions fall into two families with no analogue elsewhere: 'require*' functions (requireRole/requireUser/requireAccess/requireAdmin) that *gate* the current write, and 'access()'/'channel()'/'role()' that *mutate* the access graph (channel membership, role membership) as a side effect of processing a document - i.e., authorization state here is written by application-level script logic, not by an admin-facing grant API alone (though roles/users are still provisioned via REST API, see roles.md/users.md). The role: string-prefix convention is a notable ad hoc mechanism: one identity-argument slot is polymorphic over user vs role by lexical convention rather than a typed field, unlike Capella's credential-type-keyed privilege model.
notable_absence: There is no fixed enum of channels, roles, or 'privileges' anywhere in this API - channels and roles are freeform strings created implicitly (a channel 'comes into existence when a document is routed to it') or explicitly via REST API. This is the opposite of server/'s closed set of named RBAC privileges and Capella's closed set of management-plane roles.
